skill.name: executor-initiative
skill.description: Classify requests, draft initiative charters, and coordinate approval gates, phase transitions, and lifecycle records through the Executor workflow.
skill.summary: Manage initiative intake and lifecycle records with measurable criteria and explicit human approval.
skill.author: atri10

security_audit.summary: All 168 static alerts are false positives for their reported patterns: Markdown delimiters, sibling references, a registry lock, and routine workflow operations. Two semantic risks remain: documented unlocked transitions can lose updates, and the verification checklist can record intake approval before charter presentation. No evidence found of malware, exfiltration, or audit-directed prompt injection; referenced dependency scripts were unavailable for review.

remediation.issue: The verification checklist records an intake pass before the charter is presented for approval.
remediation.suggestion: Use read-only checks before presentation. Move the intake-pass command after explicit approval and record the approver and approval evidence.

remediation.issue: Phase and status transitions are documented as rewriting shared records without a mutex.
remediation.suggestion: Lock the full read-modify-write operation for both indexes. Use atomic writes and test concurrent transitions for lost updates.

semantic_findings.title: Verification Checklist Can Record Unapproved Intake
semantic_findings.description: The checklist says to run checks when presenting the charter, including a state-changing intake-pass command. This can record approval before the required human decision.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The checklist directly requests a pass during presentation, while the intake gate requires prior approval. Documented artifact checks do not establish human authorization.

semantic_findings.title: Concurrent Transitions Can Lose Lifecycle Records
semantic_findings.description: The skill states that phase and status updates lack locking and can lose updates in shared indexes. Prose serialization rules do not coordinate independent agents.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The source explicitly documents unlocked writes and lost updates. The dependency implementation was unavailable, so this finding concerns the documented workflow risk.

content.value_statement: Unclear scope and missing approval records make project decisions difficult to track. This skill guides request classification, charter writing, and lifecycle documentation through Executor.
actual_capabilities: Classifies requests as feasibility spikes, bounded changes, or architectural initiatives.
Guides charter writing with goals, non-goals, measurable success criteria, scope boundaries, constraints, and named approvers.
Coordinates initiative allocation and registry updates through referenced Executor scripts.
Determines whether new work fits an existing approved initiative or requires a separate initiative.
Guides phase transitions, documented skips, and lifecycle changes while preserving historical records.
Describes adoption of existing brainstorm sessions and checks for consistent initiative identifiers.
limitations: Requires the sibling Executor contract and scripts, which are not included in the two reviewed files.
Does not write specifications, plans, or implementation code; it routes those tasks to other skills.
Phase and status updates are documented as unlocked; simultaneous transitions can lose records.
Human approval remains necessary; command acceptance alone does not prove authorization.

use_cases.title: Classify an Incoming Engineering Request
use_cases.description: Determine whether a request needs a feasibility answer, a bounded change, or a documented architectural initiative.

use_cases.title: Prepare a Charter for Approval
use_cases.description: Translate an architectural request into measurable outcomes, explicit scope boundaries, and named approval responsibilities.

use_cases.title: Maintain Initiative Lifecycle Records
use_cases.description: Document approved transitions, pauses, replacements, and closure while keeping the registry and initiative index consistent.

prompt_templates.title: Classify a Request
prompt_templates.prompt: Classify this request: [request]. Explain whether it is a spike, bounded change, or architectural initiative. Do not change files.

prompt_templates.title: Draft an Initiative Charter
prompt_templates.prompt: Draft a charter for [initiative] with measurable criteria, non-goals, allowed paths, and [approver]. Present it for approval without recording a gate pass.
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate: prepare architectural work for human review.

prompt_templates.title: Evaluate Existing Initiative Scope
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare [request] with the approved charter for [initiative ID]. Recommend attachment or separate allocation without widening approved scope or changing records.

prompt_templates.title: Apply an Approved Lifecycle Transition
prompt_templates.prompt: After confirming [approval evidence], record [transition] for [initiative ID]. Serialize updates, document skipped phases, verify both indexes, and preserve prior records.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced: maintain lifecycle records using available Executor dependencies.

output_examples.input: Add multi-region failover to an initiative approved only for tenant isolation.
output: Reason: Recovery-time requirements add success criteria beyond the approved isolation scope.
Relationship: Document a dependency only if the new work genuinely depends on the existing initiative.
Existing charter: Preserve its approved scope.

best_practices: Confirm dependency availability and inspect referenced scripts before authorizing execution.
Obtain explicit approval before recording any gate pass; treat pre-presentation verification as read-only.
Serialize lifecycle updates, verify both indexes, and redact secret values from tracked documents.
anti_patterns: Create initiatives for questions or bounded changes without a lasting architectural deliverable.
Widen an approved charter or mark a gate passed without a new human decision.
Run concurrent phase updates, delete historical records, or copy example identifiers and timestamps.

faq.question: Which AI tools can use this skill?
faq.answer: The report lists Claude, Codex, and Claude Code. Full operation also requires repository access and the referenced Executor dependencies.

faq.question: Does every request need an initiative?
faq.answer: No. Feasibility spikes and most bounded changes do not. Architectural work receives an initiative or attaches to an existing approved scope.

faq.question: Can this skill implement the project?
faq.answer: No. It coordinates intake and lifecycle records. Other Executor skills handle specifications, planning, execution, verification, and handoff.

faq.question: Are the required scripts included?
faq.answer: No. The reviewed package contains instructions and examples. It references scripts and contract documents in a sibling Executor skill.

faq.question: Does a successful command prove human approval?
faq.answer: No. Explicit human approval is required. The pre-presentation verification checklist should not run a state-changing intake-pass command.

faq.question: Can multiple agents update phases simultaneously?
faq.answer: Not safely under the documented workflow. Phase and status changes lack locking, so serialize transitions and verify the resulting indexes.
